chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a woman who swore to her husband by manumission and offering (of a sacrificial animal) that she would never marry after him, and then it suited her to marry. He said: 'She sells her slave (to fulfill the oath), for I fear the ruler (will enforce it strictly) upon her, and there is nothing obligatory upon her in the truth (of the oath's core meaning). If she wishes to offer a sacrifice, she may do so.'

key_terms.السُّلْطَانَ: The ruler or authority, often implying strict enforcement of vows
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: Sacrificial animal offered during Hajj or for vows
key_terms.فِي الْحَقِّ: In the truth/correctness, referring to the core obligation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a woman's oath not to remarry after her husband's death?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the juristic principle that an oath sworn by 'manumission' (itq) is fulfilled by selling a slave rather than freeing them, a view supported by the fear of the ruler's claim to the slave's property. The Imam clarifies that while the primary obligation is satisfied through sale, the woman retains the voluntary option to offer a sacrificial animal (hady) in addition, demonstrating the flexibility in fulfilling vows within Shia fiqh. This narration underscores the distinction between the literal wording of an oath and its practical legal execution in matters of personal status.
